title: What is known about 1RB1LA_1LA1RC_1RD0RB_1LE1LD_---1LF_1RA0LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_1LA1RC_1RD0RB_1LE1LD_---1LF_1RA0LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

It is a slow counter. The tape grows only at the right end, where a solid block of 1s gains ten cells each time the run's age grows by a factor of about four; the rest of the tape, a word of 10, 110 and short blocks of 1s, changes slowly, like the higher digits of a counter. At step 4.0·108 the block was absorbed and the run restarted with a longer word: a new epoch.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1010 steps.

Where a halt would come from. The machine halts only in state E reading 0, and E is entered only from D reading 0 and stepping left. In the first 108 steps that happens 4,761,903 times and E always reads a 1.
What a proof needs. An exact description of the counter's increment and of the epoch change, showing that the cell left of a 0 that D reads is always 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 293 cells have been visited and 143 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth at the right end
claims.text: At the times the tape grows on the right, it ends b 1^k b 1 1 D>0 (b = 110), and k grows by 10 for every factor of about 4 in time: k = 71, 81, 91, 101, 111, 121, 131 at steps 403,611,844, 407,740,602, 424,255,680, 490,315,950, 754,557,084, 1,811,521,682 and 6,039,380,104.

claims.title: An epoch change
claims.text: Before step 4.02·108 the right block reached 1^119 (step 378,784,004); at step 402,235,754 the tape grows by about 100 cells within a few million steps and a new block starts from 1^2 after a longer word. Width: 153 cells at 108 steps, 292 at 109, 312 at 1010.

claims.title: E always reads 1
claims.text: E is entered only from D reading 0 (1LE); in the first 108 steps it is entered 4,761,903 times and reads a 1 every time.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.172).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The run behaves like a counter in epochs; neither the increment nor the epoch change has been described exactly.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LC_1LA1RB_1LD0LA_1RE1RD_---1RF_1LB0RF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a slow counter: the tape grows by ten cells every time the run gets four times older, with a restart on a larger scale now and then. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The block of 1s at the right end grows by 10 cells per fourfold time.
The run restarted on a larger scale at step 4.02·10<sup>8</sup>.

sections.heading: A block that grows ten cells at a time
html: Look at the right end of the tape whenever it grows. It always ends with a solid block of 1s, then 110 1 1, and the block grows by 10 cells in a burst each time the run is about four times older: 1^71 at step 403,611,844, 1^81 at 407,740,602, 1^91 at 424,255,680, 1^101 at 490,315,950, 1^111 at 754,557,084, 1^121 at 1,811,521,682, 1^131 at 6,039,380,104. Left of it is a word of 10, 110 and short blocks of 1s, which changes by a few cells per burst, like the higher digits of a counter.

The first such growth series ran until about step 3.8·108 (block 1^119). Then, around step 4.02·108, the tape grew by about a hundred cells in a few million steps, and a new series began from a short block after a longer word: a new epoch. That is the jump from 153 cells at 108 steps to 292 at 109.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The only halting transition is E reading a 0. E is entered only when D reads a 0 and steps left, so a halt needs D to read a 0 whose left neighbour is a 0. In 108 steps D reads a 0 4,761,903 times and the cell to its left is always a 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.172).
After 109 steps the tape spans 293 cells (9 left of the start, 273 right), with a density of 1s of 0.488.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A counter that grows a block of 1s at the right end by 10 cells for every fourfold increase in time; at step 4.0·10^8 it restarted on a larger scale.
